title: CI evidence of a repository
description: What the continuous integration of a repository publishes so that the status dashboard can compare what the manifest declares (evidence) with what ran. One file per repository, read from the branch and path set in dashboard-config.json (ci_evidence.branch and ci_evidence.path; by default the file ci-evidence.json on the branch ci-evidence). A repository that publishes nothing is shown as not verified.

records.description: The latest record of each workflow and kind of test. Records older than the limit of their kind (dashboard-config.json, ci_evidence.expire_days) no longer prove anything.

repo.description: Name of the repository that publishes the record. A record that names another repository is refused.

workflow.description: File name of the workflow, for example ci.yml.

branch.description: Branch that was tested. Only the default branch (main) counts.

version.description: Version of the project that was tested.

test_type.description: unit, integration and host-test prove the host-test level; simulator, bench and field prove their own.

environment.description: Where it ran, for example ubuntu-24.04, a simulator name or a bench.

bound.description: true when the run used the real hardware.

device.description: Board or machine used. Required, with bound true, for bench and field.

url.description: Link to the run, inside the repository that publishes the record.

details.description: Anything else worth keeping (numbers of tests, notes). The dashboard does not read it.
